intended_object: The canonical equivariant identification between α ∖ {a} acted on by the fixing subgroup of {a}, and α ∖ {a} acted on by the stabilizer of a (from the docstring). On paper both sides are the same set with the same group acting, so the map is the identity.
explanation:
The definition builds a map from `ofFixingSubgroup M {a}` to `ofStabilizer M a`. Both are the sub-action on the complement of {a}. The group map φ sends m to m, using the fact that fixing {a} means fixing a. The point map sends x to x, and equivariance holds by `rfl`. The next lemma, `ofFixingSubgroup_of_singleton_bijective`, proves the map is bijective.

Mathematically, the fixing subgroup of {a} is the stabilizer of a, and the two sub-actions have the same underlying set, so this map is the identity. It exists only to convert between two Lean encodings of the same object. It is a coherence device, like its neighbour `ofFixingSubgroup_of_eq`, and has no mathematical content of its own.

As a coherence map it is correct and matches its docstring: φ is well defined, the map lands in the complement of a, and it is equivariant. Nothing is restricted unnecessarily: the setting is a general group acting on a general type.
